svg.title: Animated walkthrough of Spendwise: request path through UI, Flask API, service layer and SQLite, then SQL insights, quick add, recurring payments and CI

g.text: validates the input, calls the service
service layer applies the business rules
BAD DATA IS STOPPED AT THE DATABASE, NOT JUST IN THE UI
total - LAG(total) OVER (ORDER BY month) AS change
saved through the same service layer
as the web UI and the CLI
ALL CHECKS PASSED · READY TO SHIP
Web UI and CLI call a Flask REST API, which hands off to a Python OOP service layer that owns
the business rules and talks to SQLite.
Four tables with constraints and indexes keep the data consistent and the lookups fast.
A bad row, such as a negative amount, is refused by the database itself; a valid one goes
A CTE plus LAG gives month-over-month change, so a rise or fall is a number, not a guess.
Each category is measured against its budget, and the ones that run over are flagged.
Type an expense the way you would say it. Natural-language quick add turns it into a structured
Repeating charges are detected from the history, so subscriptions and bills stand out.
Pytest checks the code, so a change is validated before it goes out.
Docker packages it, and GitHub Actions runs the checks on every push.
